title: From Expanded Carrier Screening to Dynamic and Personalised Preconceptional Genomics.
abstract: Expanded carrier screening (ECS) has substantially broadened the scope of preconception genetic screening, but the expansion of fixed gene panels has also highlighted important limitations related to population diversity, genomic coverage, variant interpretation, residual risk and the clinical value of increasingly large panels. Recent advances in population genomics, sequencing technologies, longitudinal variant reassessment, quantitative risk assessment and artificial intelligence (AI) provide opportunities to move beyond static screening models. This review examines current challenges in ECS and explores the transition towards a more dynamic and individualised framework for preconceptional genomics. Rather than continually expanding fixed panels, genomic information could be selectively interpreted within the reproductive context and reassessed as knowledge, variant classifications and individual circumstances evolve. Emerging technologies, including exome- and long-read sequencing and AI-assisted variant interpretation, may facilitate this transition, although limitations related to validation, population diversity, penetrance and clinical interpretation remain. Genetic counselling and professional oversight will therefore remain essential to ensure that increasingly complex genomic information is translated into meaningful reproductive risk assessment and informed reproductive decision-making.

title: Volumetric Digital Microsphere Assay Coupling CbAgo-CRISPR/Cas12a and Lens-Free Holography for Salmonella typhimurium Detection.
abstract: Sensitive and precise quantification of foodborne pathogens in complex matrices remains challenging due to inefficient signal conversion, limited volumetric information, and inaccurate counting under dense signal conditions. Here, we develop an integrated digital biosensing platform that combines programmable biochemical amplification, lens-free holographic imaging, and intelligent computational decoding. A CbAgo-CRISPR/Cas12a cascade is employed to convert pathogen DNA signals into discrete microsphere-based digital outputs, while automated lens-free holography preserves three-dimensional spatial information for high-throughput acquisition. A depth-guided Transformer algorithm further enables accurate three-dimensional microsphere localization in dense sensing environments. Using Salmonella typhimurium as a model pathogen, the platform exhibited a linear response from 20 to 107 CFU/mL with a detection limit of 12 CFU/mL. The method showed good selectivity against the tested nontarget bacteria and was further evaluated in spiked chicken, egg, fish, and milk matrices, yielding quantitative results in good agreement with conventional plate counting. These results demonstrate a particle-based volumetric transduction strategy for digital biosensing in complex samples.

title: EEG-MedRAG: Enhancing EEG-based Clinical Decision-Making via Hierarchical Hypergraph Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: With the widespread application of electroencephalography (EEG) in neuroscience and clinical practice, efficiently retrieving and semantically interpreting large-scale, multi-source, heterogeneous EEG data has become a pressing challenge. EEG-MedRAG addresses this challenge through a three-layer hypergraph-based retrieval-augmented generation framework that unifies EEG domain knowledge, individual patient cases, and large-scale EEG recordings into a traversable n-ary relational hypergraph, enabling joint semantic-temporal retrieval and evidence-grounded clinical reasoning. The accompanying benchmark is the first to pair EEG questions about the same clinical fact across five user roles. Its 700 questions span seven clinical domains and support direct comparisons of answer consistency across roles. Across three LLM backbones, EEG-MedRAG outperforms all four baselines in both overall answer correctness and token-level F1. It achieves up to 86.14% answer correctness on the full benchmark and 97.32% on non-EEG questions, with 97.41% evidence coverage on knowledge questions. In EEG retrieval, EEG-MedRAG improves top-five label agreement by 8.58 percentage points over the time-series baseline. The code is available at https://github.com/li-zan/EEG-MedRAG.

title: The physical foundation beneath protein generative modeling
abstract: Physical equations in protein modeling appear to have been replaced by generative models trained directly on structure data. By learning a mapping from noise to data, sampling de novo protein structures has become much more efficient. However, such models can also learn non-physical features and break down with out-of-distribution settings which are typical in protein design campaigns. In this review, we highlight where the physics persists in protein generative modeling pipelines and the issues that linger when physically relevant components of a macromolecular system are left unmodeled. We present a perspective that respecting the underlying physics of macromolecular systems, increasingly through learned representations that are physically grounded and updating generative models with experimental data, is foundational to generative modeling for functional protein design.

title: CRC tumor antigens and immune escape: Designing peptide vaccines for colorectal Cancer.
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a leading cause of global cancer mortality, with current therapies often limited by toxicity and resistance. Immunotherapy, particularly peptide-based vaccines, represents a promising alternative by eliciting targeted immune responses. This review provides a critical and comparative synthesis of CRC peptide vaccine development, distinguishing itself from previous reviews by integrating mechanistic insights into immune evasion with a structured framework that connects antigen selection, epitope identification (experimental and computational), and clinical translation. We specifically highlight two underexplored areas: tumor-associated neutrophils (TANs) and the critical distinction between microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) and microsatellite stable (MSS) CRC, which fundamentally dictates mutational burden, neoantigen load, and vaccine responsiveness. We first detail the sophisticated mechanisms of immune evasion employed by CRC, including an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment enriched with regulatory T cells (Tregs) and myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs), tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), tumor-associated neutrophils (TANs), dysregulated antigen presentation via HLA class I alterations, and expression of inhibitory checkpoints. The review critically evaluates methods for epitope identification, contrasting traditional experimental approaches with modern computational strategies that leverage genomics, AI, and immunoinformatics tools for predicting high-affinity, immunogenic epitopes. We emphasize that predicted immunogenicity does not equate to clinical efficacy, and we critically appraise the limitations of current computational tools, including high false-positive rates and poor correlation with in vivo immunogenicity. While promising, challenges remain, including low immunogenicity, human leukocyte antigen (HLA) restriction, and tumor heterogeneity. Future success likely depends on developing multi-epitope, personalized vaccines combined with adjuvants and immune checkpoint inhibitors to enhance efficacy. In conclusion, peptide vaccines offer a precise and adaptable platform for CRC immunotherapy, holding significant potential for improving clinical outcomes through targeted immune activation.

title: MINE: A Training-Free Defense against Indirect Prompt Injection via Mutual Information and Embedding Variance
abstract: Existing defenses against indirect prompt injection in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) are inherently reactive: prompt-engineering methods are often overridden by the injected instructions, while supervised detectors must be retrained for each new attack style. We propose a different paradigm: defend by maximizing relevance, not by detecting attacks. Our method, MINE, is training-free and attack-agnostic, and it also serves as a query-conditioned reranker. To evaluate defenses under realistic conditions, we introduce LC-Inj-SQuAD, a long-context benchmark with an average of 4,032 words per context. We evaluate on four datasets spanning short-context QA (Inj-SQuAD, Inj-TriviaQA), long-context QA (LC-Inj-SQuAD), and agent tool-call injection (InjecAgent). Across all four, MINE achieves the best accuracy--security trade-off among training-free defenses. It is also the only defense that stays usable against a fully adaptive attacker, generalizes to agent tool-call injection, and achieves the lowest inference latency on long contexts.

title: DRAFT-ing Architectural Design Decisions using LLMs
abstract: Architectural Knowledge Management (AKM) is crucial for software development and Architectural Decision Records (ADR), an important artifact of AKM, provide a structured approach to capture Architectural Design Decisions (ADD). However, their adoption is limited due to the manual effort involved and insufficient tool support. Prior work shows that LLMs can support ADD generation, though basic prompting yields suboptimal results. This paper explores how LLMs can support architects in two complementary tasks: generating ADDs from Decision Contexts, and generating complete ADRs from titles. We propose Domain-specific Retrieval Augmented Few-shot Tuning (DRAFT), a novel approach that integrates Retrieval Augmented Few-shot Generation with Fine-tuning to generate. DRAFT operates in two phases: an offline phase that fine-tunes a model using retrieval-augmented prompts derived from historical ADRs, and an online phase that generates decisions or complete ADRs by combining retrieved examples with the fine-tuned model. Evaluated on 4344 ADRs across multiple LLMs using standard NLP metrics, DRAFT consistently produces outputs better aligned with real-world ADRs. A human evaluation with the authors and external architects, however, shows no uniformly preferred approach. DRAFT also maintains practical efficiency, reduces dependence- dence on proprietary models, and addresses organizational concerns around privacy, resource constraints, and inference costs.

title: CA-RAG: Constraint-Aligned Retrieval for Structurally Faithful Long-Form Generation
abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) typically optimises evidence selection for semantic relevance, whereas compliance-sensitive long-form generation also requires evidence supporting explicit structural obligations. Semantically relevant retrieval may therefore omit information needed for mandatory downstream clauses. We propose Constraint-Aligned RAG (CA-RAG), a retrieval-conditioning framework that augments section-specific queries with ontology-derived structural constraints and policy-grounded knowledge-graph relations before evidence selection. Retrieval-only evaluation with manually annotated evidence shows consistent improvements across retrieval budgets. At $k=6$, CA-RAG increases Precision@$k$ from $0.5268$ to $0.5692$, pooled Recall@$k$ from $0.5402$ to $0.5950$, and F1@$k$ from $0.5389$ to $0.5672$ over standard RAG. Generation experiments further show improvements in compliance and reliability in several model--domain settings, while generation-only constraints achieve higher clause coverage but lower overall compliance and reliability. These results indicate that structurally aligned retrieval can improve evidence sufficiency in compliance-sensitive long-form generation.

title: RIBOSPAN: A Long-Context RNA Foundation Model for Versatile RNA Modeling
abstract: Full-length RNAs, particularly messenger RNAs, often exceed the context lengths used to pretrain existing RNA foundation models, limiting complete-transcript modeling at single-nucleotide resolution. We present RIBOSPAN, a 1.61-billion-parameter bidirectional RNA foundation model natively pretrained with context lengths up to 10,240 nt, combining dense bidirectional self-attention with single-nucleotide tokenization. On a controlled long-context benchmark, native long-context pretraining maintains well-organized, context-specific representations across full transcripts, an advantage that inference-time extension of short-context models does not recover. RIBOSPAN learns state-of-the-art frozen RNA representations, and is the strongest encoder-only RNA foundation model in full-transcript property prediction and zero-shot mutation-fitness modeling. Without structural supervision during pretraining, its frozen backbone outperforms a fully fine-tuned structure-guided model on secondary structure prediction. Building on the same backbone, we develop a conditional discrete-diffusion framework for full-length mRNA generation and redesign. Together, RIBOSPAN establishes a powerful long-context foundation for transferable RNA representation learning, biological prediction, and full-transcript mRNA design.

title: From Clever Hans to Hypotheses: Interpreting EEG Foundational Transformers with LRP
abstract: Emerging foundation models (FMs) in electroencephalography (EEG) promise a path to scale deep learning in diagnostics and brain-computer interfaces despite data scarcity, yet their opaque nature remains a barrier to wider adoption. We investigate attention-aware Layer-wise relevance propagation (LRP) as a post-hoc attribution method for EEG-FMs, extending LRP's use on convolutional neural network (CNN)-based EEG models to the Transformer architectures that current FMs are based on. We find that LRP can both verify EEG-FM decisions and surface novel, biologically plausible hypotheses from them. In motor imagery, it unmasks 'Clever Hans' behavior where models prioritize task correlated ocular signals over the intended motor correlates. In a naturalistic paradigm for affect prediction, it reveals a recurring reliance on a central electrode cluster, suggesting a candidate sensorimotor signature of arousal. Though heatmap interpretation remains ambiguous in this complex domain, the results position LRP as a tool for both verification and exploration of EEG-FMs, a role that will grow in both importance and discovery potential as the underlying models mature.

title: GEM: A Generative Embedding Model Bridging Reasoning and Retrieval
abstract: Modern LLMs excel at reasoning and instruction following, enabling users to express increasingly complex information needs. However, existing retrievers largely rely on matching surface-level relevance, creating a growing gap between the evolving nature of user queries and how the queries are interpreted by retrievers. In this paper, we present GEM, a generative embedding model that augments retrieval by leveraging its internal knowledge to reason about user intent and relevance criteria prior to embedding. GEM unifies generation and embedding in a sequential manner, where encoding can be conceptually viewed as processing only one additional token during autoregressive generation. Unlike conventional query expansion, GEM learns to produce embeddings aligned with its reasoning, moving beyond surface-level matching. Furthermore, the generative nature allows GEM to be prompted like standard instruction-tuned LLMs and enables test-time compute scaling for retrieval. Compared with a non-reasoning variant of the same backbone, GEM achieves approximately 35% relative improvement in nDCG@10 on BRIGHT, a benchmark of challenging queries requiring reasoning, and 70% in p-MRR on FollowIR, a benchmark evaluating retrievers' ability to understand and follow user instructions. Our results demonstrate the effectiveness of activating an embedding model's internal reasoning capabilities to improve retrieval. Our code and model are publicly available at https://github.com/ZhlSh17/GEM and https://huggingface.co/gem-search/GEM-4B, respectively.

title: From Head to Tail: LLM-Augmented Sequential Recommendation and Trade-off Optimization
abstract: Recommender systems exhibit popularity bias, often under-serving long-tail and cold-start items with sparse interaction data. We propose a group-specific data augmentation approach that leverages LLMs to generate synthetic interactions, formulated as a constrained optimization problem, maximizing group-specific NDCG@20 and coverage while bounding overall NDCG@20 degradation within an acceptable threshold. Items are partitioned by interaction frequency to find the optimal augmentation strategy for each group. We further study combining the augmentation across groups simultaneously and find that while individual optimal strategies navigate the multi-group augmentation design, they are not simply additive. We further ablate on the LLM-based augmentation itself, comparing LLM scales, augmentation configuration under token constraints, finding that augmentation quality scales with contextual richness, albeit at a proportionally higher cost. Experiments with SASRec demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, achieving over 100% and 60% improvement in group-specific NDCG@20 for extreme and regular long-tail items, respectively, on our industrial dataset, and 40%, 25% for MovieLens-32M, while increasing their coverage without significant overall degradation.

title: Experiment-as-Code Labs: A Declarative Stack for AI-Driven Scientific Discovery
abstract: To unleash the full potential of AI for Science, we must untether the agents from a purely digital environment. The agent's ability to control and explore in real-world labs is essential because the physical lab remains foundational to scientific discovery. While some tasks can be performed on a computer (e.g., data analysis, running simulated experiments), Eureka moments could occur at any time while operating lab instruments (e.g., when a scientist notices unexpected clues, intuition may prompt a real-time course change). Although autonomous labs are on the rise, which expose programmable APIs to control scientific instruments via software, bridging the gap between increasingly powerful AI agents and automated lab equipment requires innovation that draws insights from computer systems. We propose a new paradigm called ``Experiment-as-Code (EaC) Labs,'' where a core concept is to encode experiments as declarative configurations that can be compiled down to device-level APIs. AI agents come up with hypotheses and experiments, written as an ensemble of declarative configurations. The systems layer performs program analysis, safety checks, resource assignment, and job orchestration. Finally, programmatic experimentation occurs via actuating the device APIs. This is a general stack that is science-, lab-, and instrument-independent, representing a novel synthesis across the physical, systems, and intelligence layers to unleash the next breakthrough in AI for Science.

title: RAVEN: A Self-RAG Based Agent for Threat Classification and Response
abstract: Security event analysis in large enterprises can be overwhelming, as each alert typically requires manual in- spection by human operators. This process is time-consuming and prone to inconsistencies, especially in high-volume Secu- rity Operations Center (SOC) environments. In this work- in-progress paper, we present RAVEN: Retrieval-Augmented Vulnerability & Event aNalysis, an agentic framework designed to support SOC analysts by automating the initial stages of alert investigation. The proposed system leverages a Self- Reflective Retrieval-Augmented Generation-based approach to provide an initial classification of security events and enables interactive refinement through analyst-in-the-loop queries. Un- like traditional approaches that rely on generic mitigation strategies, RAVEN generates context-aware remediation sug- gestions by incorporating knowledge of the target enterprise infrastructure. We implement an early-stage prototype and report preliminary results on three balanced test sets of 400 curated web payloads each (SQLi, XSS, SSTI) and a qualitative case study of mitigation generation; an evaluation on IDS- generated alerts and a user study are ongoing and outlined as remaining work.

title: SuSi-RAG: A Hybrid Graph RAG for Equipment Maintenance
abstract: In the manufacturing domain, equipment maintenance tasks depend on expert knowledge. Their documentation is often stored in heterogeneous formats and sources. The enhancement of LLMs with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is promising for bridging the scattered knowledge, but traditional vector-based RAG shows weaknesses with two characteristics which are common in real maintenance queries: complex causal chains and cross-domain synthesis. To address this, we propose SuSi-RAG, a hybrid Graph RAG solution, that matches a user query and each maintenance record using subgraph similarity. This work shows an in-use system: SuSi-RAG has run on an active Bosch production line for more than eight months, handling 10,664 question-answer interactions and demonstrates upper bound answer accuracy of 96.25% (confirmed error rate 3.75%). In a proof-of-concept, SuSi-RAG improves top-1 retrieval accuracy from 61.5% to 96.2% and expert-rated answer quality from 44.9% to 84.1% against a vector-based baseline. We present an integrated operational feedback loop to update SuSi-RAG.
